title: [Full Workshop] Llama 3 at 1,000 tok/s on the SambaNova AI Platform
talk_summary: A SambaNova vendor workshop pitching their full-stack hardware platform (RDU chip, 3-tier memory) and 'Samba-1' composition-of-experts product that routes prompts across many fine-tuned expert models behind one endpoint, plus a hands-on LangChain/RAG tutorial against their Llama 3 endpoint.

takeaways.technique: Single endpoint over a pool of expert models with a router
takeaways.what_they_do: They expose many task-specialized models behind one secure endpoint and route each incoming prompt to the best-suited expert, with fallbacks to direct model calls or model chaining for agentic flows.
takeaways.evidence_quote: we're delivering the ability to determine based off of an incoming prompt, what is the best suited expert behind the scenes to solve that prompt

takeaways.what_they_do: Model-level RBAC so a given app, person, or group can only reach a defined subset of models, giving compute efficiency plus fine-grained control.
takeaways.evidence_quote: this application or this person or this group of people should be able to access this set of models

takeaways.technique: Chunk size/overlap tuning with explicit config
takeaways.what_they_do: They expose chunk size and overlap as config hyperparameters (1200/240) and report chunk counts, so retrieval quality is tunable per document type.
takeaways.evidence_quote: I set the, uh, chunk size to 1,200, and then the, uh, chunk overlap to 240, but again, you can change those configs

takeaways.what_they_do: They default to a simple PDF loader but recommend swapping to an 'unstructured' loader when documents contain complex tables, driven by a single config flag.
takeaways.evidence_quote: if you end up having like more complicated tables in PDF, in this case, I would recommend to switch to the unstructured data loader
